messages:
marie: quick heads-up — since the rollout yesterday we've seen a spike in SLO notifications for a handful of mid-tier tenants. most are noisy low-priority alerts during traffic spikes. wondering if we can do better with routing + quiet windows per-tenant.

 dan: can you paste an example of the noisy rule? is this mostly error-rate or latency?

 marie: mostly 5m latency p95 > 350ms for a route that degrades under load. tenant A/B keep firing during warmup leading to duplicate pages.

 alex: +1 — looks like our notify router treats all tenants same precedence. we only have global quiet windows and then an emergency bypass. that means mid-tier tenants get paged even when the signal is expected.

 jess: UX Q: would per-tenant quiet windows be exposed in console or hidden behind an API? exposing per-tenant knobs could be confusing for SREs and account owners.

 marie: proposal: add two soft fields to notify rules: `quiet_window` (seconds) and `priority_tier` (low|normal|critical). by default inherit org-level. routing policy uses priority_tier to decide escalation and quiet_window to suppress repeated pages within window unless `critical` or a distinct fingerprint.

 alex: example config we sketched in router service: ```json
{"route": "/api/search","slo": {"p95_ms": 350,"quiet_window_s": 600,"priority_tier": "normal"},"tenant": "tenant-a"}
```

 ryan: oncall note: we can't silently drop alerts that indicate real degradation. any suppression must still generate a silent console entry + aggregated metric for postmortem. Otherwise we lose signal.

 marie: agreed. behavior: suppressed alerts -> create `suppressed_alert` event (no page) with link to raw signal + count. console shows a small badge and a collapsed timeline.

 dan: think about quota/limits too — per-tenant quiet windows could be abused to hide problems. maybe allow slack window only up to org SLA threshold + require owner override with audit log.

 alex: implementation plan: router changes + console UI for rule editor + telemetry (suppressed vs paged counts). aim for prototype behind feature-flag for a small cohort.

 jess: mock idea: in rule editor add a compact dropdown: Quiet window: Off / 1m / 5m / 10m / Custom (seconds). Priority: Low / Normal / Critical. show a tooltip: "Suppressed alerts still recorded in timeline".

 marie: risks: rollback could cause alert storm if we flip flags globally. mitigation: gradual rollout + canary tenants + burstbackoff circuit breaker.

 oncall-bot: deploy-bot: new branch `notify/quiet-windows` deployed to staging at 2026-03-19T16:42:10Z :rocket:

 dan: action items: 1) alex to open RFC + proto PR (this week). 2) jess to mock console UX (EOW). 3) marie to prepare rollout checklist and canary tenant list. 4) ryan to write oncall runbook updates about suppressed events.

 marie: timeline sounds good. tagging folks — @alex @jess @ryan please ack when you have PR/mocks. i'll start a short RFC and include expected telemetry dims (tenant, route, priority_tier, suppressed_count, paged_count).

 alex: ack, will open RFC and a tiny router change PR today.

 jess: ack — mock up by friday and will share in #design.

 ryan: ack — will add runbook entries and verification steps.

 marie: thanks. if no objections i'll put the RFC up by EOD and mark it experimental. :thumbsup:
